title: Bug: Nested providers for the same context will lead to unnecessary render calls when only the outside context value changed  (React 19 only)
body:
Since React 19, nested providers for the same context will lead to unnecessary render calls for some scenarios. I wrote a unit test and confirmed that React 18.3.1 behaves as expected.

E.g. for the following pseudo-code React component structure:
```tsx
<SomeContextProvider>
  <SomeContextConsumer>
    <SomeContextProvider>
      <SomeContextConsumer />
    </SomeContextProvider>
  </SomeContextConsumer>
</SomeContextProvider>
```
If the value provided by the outer SomeContextProvider changes, the innermost SomeContextConsumer will also be rendered. (Actually it will only "semi-render", because even though the function is called, the result is ignored.)

It is probably only an unnecessary detail for most users, but for me it broke some tests which track every single render for performance reasons and it actually causes >1k unnecessary component function calls in some situations because I utilize some nested contexts for some widely used information where it is important that elements are only rerendered when the context value changes. So if the top-level context provider is updated, but another provider between the element and it is not updated, the element should not be rendered.  
Also, it is very concerning that it executes the component function but ignores the result.

React version: 19.2.3 (and 19.0.0)
Works in 18.3.1

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Open code example below. Execute `vitest` in terminal.
  - The test will fail, because the component was kind of rendered, even though it was unnecessary.
2. Downgrade to React 18.3.1 by updating package.json and running `npm install`
3. Execute `vitest` in terminal. The test will pass.

Link to code example:

[Repro code in unit test on Stackblitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-tests-browser-examples-akwsn1xm?file=tests%2Freact19ContextsBugMinimalReprodWithUnitTest.test.tsx)

## The current behavior
The inner component consuming the React context is called, even though the context value has not changed for it.

title: Agents: Open in VS Code on a Dev Container environment hangs when the Docker context is not `default`
body:
Testing #349554

**Open in VS Code** on a session in a Dev Container environment never connects when the Docker CLI's active context is not `default`. The editor window stays on **Opening Remote...** while Dev Containers retries `docker version` against `/var/run/docker.sock`.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No. The Dev Containers extension resolves the editor window.

- VS Code Version: 1.148.0-insider (`ade7f1b62fe6890ef4fee08ea5a8ebb0e7c002f8`), Dev Containers 0.479.0 (pre-release)
- OS Version: macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Docker Desktop (engine 29.8.2). The active CLI context is `desktop-linux`, and `/var/run/docker.sock` does not exist.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.devContainer.environments.enabled`.
2. In **Manage Remote Environments**, choose **Group By** > **Type**, then **Create Dev Container** on the **Dev Containers** group. Wait for **Connected**.
3. Start a session in the new environment (folder `/workspaces/<name>`) and send any prompt.
4. Use **Open in VS Code Editor Window** (⇧⌘A).

**Actual:** The new window titled `<name>` stays on **Opening Remote...**. I waited more than 6 minutes, including a window reload. The Dev Containers log repeats:

```
Context:           default
failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: connect: no such file or directory
...
Stop (30245 ms): Check Docker is running
Docker returned an error code 1, message: Command failed: docker version
```

**Expected:** The window opens `/workspaces/<name>` in the container the agent host created, with the session in Chat.

**Cause:** The agent host runs Docker in the CLI's active context (`desktop-linux`), so the container lives on that engine. The authority built by [`resolveRemoteAgentHostEntryAuthority`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ade7f1b62fe6890ef4fee08ea5a8ebb0e7c002f8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/op

title: Test: HTTP sign-in and page dialogs in the integrated browser
body:
Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300149, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/347876, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/349503, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/349555

- [x] anyOS @osortega
- [x] anyOS @dbaeumer

Complexity: 3


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23349584%0A%0A&assignees=kycutler)

---

The integrated browser now asks you to sign in to sites that use HTTP Basic authentication, and pages can use `prompt()`. JavaScript dialogs also now wait until their browser is visible, and agents can answer them.

## Setup

> [!TIP]
> I'd recommend linking this TPI to an agent and asking it to create an HTML harness to help walk through the scenarios.

- A local page served over `http://localhost` with buttons that call `alert()`, `confirm()`, and `prompt()`, both immediately and after a few seconds' delay, and that show what each call returned. Add two `sandbox` iframes that call `prompt()`, one with `allow-modals` and one without.
- For sign-in, use `https://httpbin.org/basic-auth/user/passwd` (username `user`, password `passwd`) and its `http://` version.

## Scenarios

### Sign-in
- Open the `https://` httpbin URL. Ensure that a **Sign in to …** dialog asks for a username and password, and that the page loads after you log in.
- Enter the wrong credentials, then cancel. Ensure that the site's unauthorized response shows instead of a page that hangs.
- Open the `http://` httpbin URL. Ensure that the dialog warns that your connection isn't secure.
- Embed the httpbin URL in an iframe on your local page. No sign-in dialog should appear for it, because only the page's own site can ask.

- [x] anyOS @vritant24 (editor and Agents window)
- [x] ssh @benibenj (remote agent host)

Complexity: 4
Authors: @meganrogge
Testing milestone: **1.148.0**


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23349544%0A%0A&assignees=meganrogge)

---

## Setup

Use the latest Insiders and **disposable repositories only**. Create agent sessions using worktrees, including one with changes you can safely discard. Have a connected remote agent host with its own test worktrees.

Run **Open Worktree Cleanup** from the Command Palette in both the regular editor and Agents window.

## Test

- In the editor, close or hide the chat/session views, then open cleanup. Expect the same usable inventory and cleanup controls as in the Agents window. Sessions outside the editor's current workspace must not make their worktrees look unused.
- Find both local and remote worktrees. Expect clear host identity, including when two hosts have the same directory path. Selecting a remote worktree must affect only that host.
- Select an unused worktree and cancel the confirmation. Nothing should be removed. Confirm cleanup on another: expect useful progress, removal from disk and `git worktree list`, and the branch to remain.
- Repeat with tracked and untracked changes. Expect the changes to remain recoverable on the retained branch. Try a worktree still in use: cleanup must respect its safety checks rather than deleting it blindly.
- Disconnect the remote host before cleanup completes, then reconnect and refresh. Expect unavailable/pending state, not a false success. A failed cleanup should explain the problem and remain available for retry.
- Use the keyboard to select, confirm, cancel, and read progress. Check Accessibility Help and screen-reader labels if available.
- With AI features disabled, the cleanup command should not be offered.

title: Agent picker: hide agents that use experimental vscode: options unless selected
body:
﻿Agent files can set VS Code-only options under a `vscode:` key, for example `welcome-message`. These options are experimental. They are meant for agents that an extension opens itself, e.g. with `workbench.action.newChatWindow { mode }` (see Team Tools' Agent Fix, microsoft/vscode-packages#453).

Today such agents also show up in every agent picker, next to general-purpose agents, although they only make sense when opened by their extension.

**Proposal:** an agent that uses any `vscode:` option is offered in the agent picker only while it is selected. It stays selectable by name (mode argument, `/agent`), and a chat opened with it shows it in its picker.

## Request

Please give extensions a supported way to show a given chat session where it already lives:

- if the session is showing in the Chat view or has a chat editor tab, reveal it there;

title: RSC request to a dynamic segment with notFound() loops on 307 (_rsc) until ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, then falls back to browser navigation
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

REPLACE_WITH_MINIMAL_REPRO_URL

### To Reproduce

1. Build and start in production: next build, then next start (also seen with output: 'standalone').
2. Open any page that has the client router, for example /hu/termekek/.
3. In the browser console run: window.next.router.push('/hu/termekek/does-not-exist/'). A Link to such a URL behaves the same.
4. Watch the Network tab.

The route is app/[locale]/termekek/[slug]/page.tsx. It has generateStaticParams() that returns the known slugs, and it calls notFound() for an unknown slug.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current:

1. The RSC request GET /hu/termekek/does-not-exist/?_rsc=HASH returns 307 with Location: .../?_rsc (no value).
2. Every following request goes to .../?_rsc&_rsc=HASH and returns 307 again. This repeats about 20 times, until Chrome reports net::ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.
3. The client logs "Failed to fetch RSC payload for URL. Falling back to browser navigation." and loads the page normally, which returns 404 and the not-found page.

The visitor ends up on the correct page, but only after about 20 wasted requests and console errors.

Expected: a single RSC response (for example the not-found payload) or one redirect, with no loop.

Notes:
- dynamicParams = true or false makes no difference.
- The app proxy.ts returns no 307 (it only returns 301, 400 and 410).
- An unknown path that is handled by a catch-all app/[locale]/[...rest]/page.tsx (which calls notFound()) returns one clean 200 RSC response, so the loop is specific to the dynamic segment that uses generateStaticParams.
- A hand-made curl with the header rsc: 1 returns 307 even for valid pages, because the _rsc hash is missing. That is expected and is not the bug.
- Possibly related: #99568 (also an _rsc redirect loop on Link navigation, but caused by a layout redirect with middleware).

### Provide environment information

Next.js 16.4.5, React 19.3.1, Node 24.6.0, macOS.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Amanar-Marouane/next-turbopack-dynamic-fs-access

Made with `npx create-next-app -e reproduction-template`. I added one route handler and `output: "standalone"`. Nothing else.

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo above
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run build`
4. The build prints `Turbopack build encountered 3 warnings`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** One small route handler produces three `Dynamic filesystem access causes tracing of the whole project` warnings. Two of them point here:

```ts
if (path.dirname(path.resolve(target)) !== path.resolve(dir)) {
```

They land on `20:20` and `20:46`, the two `path.resolve` calls inside that comparison. The line does not touch the disk. `path.join`, `path.resolve` and `path.dirname` only build strings. The two results get compared and that is it.

The third one is `16:18`, on `path.join(dir, file)`. `dir` comes from `UPLOAD_DIR`, a mounted volume outside the project, so its value is only known at runtime. The first suggestion ("make sure the path is statically scoped to some subfolder") cannot apply there.

**Expected.** Only calls that really reach the filesystem should warn, `writeFile`, `readdir`, `unlink` and so on. Path arithmetic that feeds a comparison should not.

If it has to warn anyway, one opt out for the directory would be better than one per call. As it stands the only way to silence it is `path.resolve(/*turbopackIgnore: true*/ ...)`, and that comment has to sit on the check that stops requests from escaping `UPLOAD_DIR`. Putting a suppression on the safety check is backwards.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [x] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Version: macOS 15.7.9
Binaries:
  Node: 22.19.0
  npm: 10.x
Relevant packages:
  next: 15.5.28 (emission code verified unchanged in 16.4.6 / 16.5.0-canary.50)
  react: 19.x
  next-auth: 5.0.0-beta
```

### Which example does this report relate to?

N/A — dev-server (webpack) internals, `FlightClientEntryPlugin.createActionAssets`

### What browser are you using? (if relevant)

N/A

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

N/A — affects `next dev` locally

### Describe the Bug

On a large App Router application (~170 routes), `next dev` (webpack) crash-loops with:

```
RangeError: Invalid string length
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
```

The throw happens in `createActionAssets()` (`dist/build/webpack/plugins/flight-client-entry-plugin.js`) when it stringifies the accumulated `serverManifest` — `server-reference-manifest.json` reaches **~625MB**, exceeding V8's maximum string length (536,870,911 bytes).

Externally this presents as the dev server repeatedly dying and restarting; POSTs to Server Actions return 404s/connection resets while the process is down, which silently broke our e2e coverage for every mutation (the pages themselves still served from the partially-restarted server).

The growth is multiplicative, not linear:

- Each entry in `serverActions[id].workers` holds a `{ moduleId, async }` object **per referencing entrypoint**, so the table is O(actions × routes).
- Worker payloads repeat verbatim: every action exported by the same module gets an identical action-entry-loader request per page, so the same `{ moduleId, async }` object is emitted thousands of times. Dev `moduleId`s are long request strings.
- In dev the JSON is pretty-printed (`JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)`), roughly doubling the size.
- `edgeServerManifest` is then stringified

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

Not public yet. The failing app is private. I have traces and a probe that dumps React root lanes on failure, described below. I haven't reduced it to a public reproduction.

### To Reproduce

1. Production build on Vercel preview, Next 16.4.0, `cacheComponents: true`, `exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild` on for the test build. React 19.2.8, `@next/playwright` 16.4.0, Playwright 1.62.0, Chromium.
2. One test opens an authenticated dashboard, then visits about 50 navigation-drawer destinations in order. For each it opens the drawer, enters `instant()`, clicks the `<Link>` (`prefetch={false}`), waits for the URL, and asserts the prefetched shell. After the scope ends it waits for the streamed page, then clicks a header `<Link>` back to the dashboard without the lock.
3. In some runs, one click never commits. Which destination stalls varies between runs: `/invoices`, `/courses`, `/customers`, `/metrics`, `/admin/dashboard`. Some of these have their own `loading.tsx`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expected: the URL changes and the prefetched shell renders inside the `instant()` callback.

Current: the URL stays on the previous page until the 20 s wait times out. In a failing run:

- Before the lock is acquired, the React root has no pending lanes (`pendingLanes = 0`).
- After the click, the locked-navigation prefetch (`_tree` plus segment requests) and the dynamic RSC request all return 200.
- The router finishes the navigation. When the scope is released, the instant cookie already holds the captured-SPA value (`[1, …, {from, to}]`), so `updateCapturedSPAToTree` ran.
- React never commits. The root has two transition lanes pending, entangled with each other and suspended, and not pinged. `cancelPendingCommit` is `null`, stylesheets and fonts are loaded, and no resource request is pending.
- No `history.pushState`, no console error, no page error.

Expected: gzip like pages, since `compress` is on and the body is JSON. Cause: `sendResponse` (`server/send-response.ts`) copies the Response headers with `NodeNextResponse.appendHeader` (`server/base-http/node.ts`), which always calls `setHeader(name, [...current, value])`. So `Content-Type` is stored as `['application/json']`. The compression middleware applied in `router-server` checks `compressible(res.getHeader('Content-Type'))`, which expects a string, so the response is filtered out. Logging `res.getHeader('content-type')` in `writeHead` shows the array. Storing a single value as a string (array only from the second value) fixes it; we run that as a patch: ```js appendHeader(name, value) { const currentValues = this.getHeaderValues(name) if (currentValues === undefined) { this._res.setHeader(name, value) } else if (!currentValues.includes(value)) { this._res.setHeader(name, [...currentValues, value]) } return this } ``` ### Provide environment information Next.js 16.4.2 (same code in 16.4.5), Node 26, Linux and macOS, `next start` behind an AWS ALB (no CDN). Seen with both Turbopack and webpack builds. ### Which area(s) are affected?

title: Turbopack: webpack-loader pool processes stay alive (and hold their heap) after compilation, through "Collecting page data" and "Generating static pages"
body:
### What happens

During `next build` with `reactCompiler: true`, Turbopack starts one webpack-loader pool for the React Compiler's Babel transform, sized to `available_parallelism()`. The pool processes (`pool_entry-[turbopack-node]_transforms_webpack-loaders_ts_*.js`) each grow to about 370-560 MB RSS during compilation. Compilation ends ("Compiled successfully"), but the pool processes are not shut down: they stay alive and idle, holding that memory, until the whole build exits. Static generation then starts its own workers on top of them.

Measured in a Docker build (Linux VM, 8 CPUs, next 16.4.4, a production App Router app, process tree sampled every 2 s inside the VM):

| phase | loader pool | static workers (6) | `next-build` main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| compile | 8 processes, about 3.4 GB | none | about 2.1 GB |
| static generation | still 8 processes, about 3.4 GB, idle | about 2.6-3.1 GB | about 2.5 GB |

The peak of the build is the sum of all three, about 8 GB. With `reactCompiler: false` (and `TURBO_TASKS_AVAILABLE_PARALLELISM=2`) there is no loader pool at all and the same build peaks about 3 GB lower. With the CPUs pinned to 2 (`taskset -c 0-1`), the pool is 2 processes, about 0.8 GB, still alive through static generation.

This is not #100064 (one pool per loader chain and context): here there is a single pool, at the expected size; the problem is its lifetime.

### Expected

The loader pool is shut down (or shrunk to zero) once compilation finishes, before "Collecting page data", so static-generation workers get that memory. On small build machines (a 4 GB CI runner or Docker VM) this is the difference between a build that fits and one that swaps until it stalls.

### Repro

Any app with `reactCompiler: true` and enough modules for the loader processes to grow; sample `ps -eo rss,args` every second during `next build` and watch the `webpack-loaders` processes after "Compiled successfully".

body:
## Link to the code that reproduces this issue

The full reproduction is inline under "To Reproduce" below (no separate repository): one `"use cache"` function with `cacheTag("t")`, a Route Handler calling `revalidateTag("t", { expire: 0 })`, and a script that starts `next start` with `Date.now` shifted via `--require`.

## To Reproduce

1. App Router, `cacheComponents: true`, default cache handlers (no `cacheHandlers` config).
2. `lib/data.ts`:
   ```ts
   export async function getValue() {
     "use cache";
     cacheTag("t");
     cacheLife({ stale: 60, revalidate: 300, expire: 86400 });
     return (await fetch(BACKEND)).json();
   }
   ```
   A dynamic route (`await connection()`) renders `getValue()`.
3. A Route Handler `POST /api/revalidate` calls `revalidateTag("t", { expire: 0 })` and returns 204.
4. `next build`, then start the server with the wall clock shifted relative to the monotonic clock, for example:
   `node --require ./shift.cjs .next/standalone/server.js`, where `shift.cjs` is `const r = Date.now; Date.now = () => r() - 5000;`
   This is what happens on WSL2 or after an NTP/chrony step or a VM pause. We measured jumps of about 1.9 s within 30 s on WSL2.
5. Loop: change the backend value, `POST /api/revalidate` (204), then immediately GET the page.

## Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected** (docs for `revalidateTag`, `{ expire: 0 }`): "Stale content is never served, so the next request is a blocking revalidate/cache miss."

**Current:**
- If `Date.now()` is **behind** `performance.timeOrigin + performance.now()`: an entry created less than the drift before the call is neither expired nor stale. It is served indefinitely, until a later revalidation arrives more than the drift after the entry was created.
- If `Date.now()` is **ahead**: the entry is marked stale but not expired, so the first request(s) are served the old value (stale-while-revalidate) despite `expire: 0`.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/sustinbebustin/next-safari27-back-skip

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start`
2. In Safari 27.0 (macOS 26.7.1), open a new window and paste `http://localhost:3000/items/a` into the address bar, so it is the first history entry.
3. Click **Items** in the nav. This is a `<Link>` to `/items`.
4. Click **Item b**. The row calls `router.push("/items/b")`, is not prefetched, and the page awaits 1.5s.
5. Press Safari's Back button.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** Back lands on `/items`.

**Current:** Back lands on `/items/a`, and `/items` is skipped. `navigation.entries()` still lists `/items`, but it is missing from the Back button's long-press menu. `history.back()` is not affected, only the browser Back button and Cmd-[.

Safari 27 flags a history entry as "created by JS without user interaction" when `pushState` runs outside the click's user-activation window. In practice that is about 1s or more after the click, or after an awaited fetch. Back from a flagged entry also skips the entry before it (see `WebBackForwardList::itemStartingAtIndexSkippingItemsAddedByJSWithoutUserGesture` in WebKit). The App Router writes the new entry in `HistoryUpdater`'s `useInsertionEffect` after the RSC response arrives, so every non-prefetched navigation produces a flagged entry in Safari 27.

We first hit this in a production app and isolated it there with automated Safari runs, one run each, all deterministic:

| How the entry was added | Back result |
|---|---|
| `history.pushState` in the click handler, or setTimeout 300–600ms | correct |
| `history.pushState` after `await fetch()` + 600ms (about 1.1s total) | skips |
| `history.pushState` after setTimeout 1500ms | skips |
| `router.push` to a dynamic route, not prefetched (push after RSC fetch, 0.2–0.9s) | skips |
| `router.push` to a dynamic route after `router.prefetch(href)` (default kind) | skips |
| `router.push` afte

| 16.4.2 | 6.3 min | 5–7 GB |
| 16.4.4 | 8.1 min | 5.1 GB |
| 16.4.4 with `reactCompiler: false` | 8.1 min | 4.9 GB |
| 16.5.0-canary.21 | slow | – |
| 16.5.0-canary.23 | fast (~13 s) | – |
| 16.5.0-canary.36 | 12.4 s | 4.6 GB |

- The first ~1 minute uses all cores; then the build runs a long, single-threaded tail (one core at 100 %) for the rest of the time.
- It is not the React Compiler: the time is identical with it switched off.
- Everything after the compile step (TypeScript, page data, etc.) takes seconds and is not affected.
- On a hosted build (Amplify Hosting, 8 GB) the same compile took 18–29 minutes and was finally killed with `signal: 9 (SIGKILL)` in the Node subprocess ("Node.js subprocess crashed while evaluating loaders [next/dist/build/babel/loader]"); with 16 GB it completes in about 25 minutes in total.

### App size

About 56 pages, 26 route handlers and ~3,000 source files (`.ts`/`.tsx`), App Router, `output` not standalone, with `@sentry/nextjs` (`withSentryConfig`), `reactCompiler` in production, `turbopack.debugIds: true`, `experimental.serverSourceMaps: true`. We did not test without the Sentry wrapper.

### What we know about the fix

The slowdown disappears somewhere between 16.5.0-canary.21 (slow) and 16.5.0-canary.23 (fast). We first suspected "Turbopack: loader change invalidation" (#95732, reverted in 16.4.3 by #100438) but 16.4.3 and 16.4.4 are still slow, so that was not it

title: next/font: no `<link rel="preload" as="font">` is emitted when `cacheComponents` is enabled
body:
### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

With `cacheComponents: true`, `<link rel="preload" as="font">` tags are not emitted for
fonts loaded via `next/font/google` in the root layout. CSS `<link rel="stylesheet">` and
JS preload tags for the same route are still emitted correctly, so the omission is
specific to fonts.

The font URLs *are* computed — they appear in the RSC flight stream as hoistable-link
hints:

```
:HL["/_next/static/media/4a0b7dd978568ff2-s.p.…woff2","font",{"crossOrigin":"","type":"font/woff2"}]
```

but never as `<link>` elements in the served `<head>`. A flight hint is only acted on
once the client hydrates, which is too late to affect the initial paint: the browser
discovers the fonts only after downloading and parsing the CSS that holds the
`@font-face` rules.

**Expected behavior**

Per the [Preloading docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/font#preloading),
a font called in the root layout "is preloaded on all routes". That holds with
`cacheComponents` disabled and stops holding when it is enabled.

### To Reproduce

Toggling **only** `cacheComponents` on an otherwise unchanged project flips the behavior:

| `next.config.ts` | `grep -c 'as="font"' .next/server/app/index.html` |
| --- | --- |
| `cacheComponents: false` | **2** |
| `cacheComponents: true` | **0** |

Steps:

1. App Router project with `next/font/google` called in `app/layout.tsx`, applied with the
   `variable` pattern:

   ```ts
   const interTight = Inter_Tight({ variable: "--font-inter-tight", weight: ["400","500","600"], subsets: ["latin"], display: "swap" });
   // …
   <html className={`${interTight.variable} …`}>
   ```

2. `next.config.ts` with `cacheComponents: true`.
3. `next build && next start`
4. `curl -s http://localhost:3000/ | grep 'rel="preload".*font'` → prints nothing.
5. Set `cacheComponents: false` (and `partialPrefetching: false`, which requires it),
   remove any `"use cache"` usage, rebuild → the two preload tags app

title: Soft navigation waits for the target's in-flight segment prefetch (page head) instead of showing loading.js (regression in 16.3.1-canary.16, still in 16.4.3)
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/timson-js/next-head-blocks-navigation-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, then `npm run build && npm start` (serves on `http://localhost:3100`).
2. In another terminal, run `node measure.mjs 5` (Playwright, Chromium).
   - The script opens `/`, which has a single `<Link href="/target">` with the default prefetch.
   - It waits until the `/_tree` prefetch for `/target` has arrived, then clicks the link while
     the segment-data prefetch for `/target` is still in flight.
   - To make that window deterministic, it delays only non-`/_tree` prefetch requests by 3 s,
     standing in for a slow network or a busy prefetch queue. The navigation request is not delayed.
3. The script prints, per click, the time until the URL changes, until `app/target/loading.js`
   is shown, and until the page content is shown.

`/target` is dynamic (`await connection()` plus a 1.2 s delay) and has its own `loading.js`.
The root layout exports a static `metadata`. There is no other config.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected** (and what 16.3.8 does): the click commits right away. The URL changes and
`loading.js` is shown within about 70 ms, then the page replaces it once the navigation
response arrives, about 1.2 s later.

**Current** (16.3.1-canary.16 through 16.4.3 and 16.5.0-canary.34): nothing happens on screen
until the delayed **prefetch** resolves. The URL stays on `/`, `loading.js` is never shown,
and the page appears only when the prefetch finishes, even though the navigation response
arrived after about 1.2 s.

Five runs each, `PREFETCH_DELAY_MS=3000`:

| `next`           | URL change (median) | `loading.js` shown | content (median) |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| 16.3.8           | 71 ms               | 5/5                | 1242 ms          |
| 16.4.3           | 2748 ms             | 0/5                | 2748 ms          |

title: turbopackSharedRuntime: true emits an inline bootstrap script that violates strict script-src CSPs
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/99504

### To Reproduce

- Next.js 16.4.3, Pages Router, next build with Turbopack.
- Default configuration: Served HTML for a page contains one inline <script> without src
- Same app built with next build --webpack: zero inline executable scripts.
- Same app built with Turbopack and experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime: false: zero inline 

### Current vs. Expected behavior

## Actual
With `experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` at its default `true` on Canary, a production Turbopack build of a Pages Router app emits an executable inline `<script>` with no `src` and no nonce:

```html
<script>(globalThis["TURBOPACK"] || (globalThis["TURBOPACK"] = [])).push({"otherChunks": [...], "runtimeModuleIds": [...]});</script>
```

Under a strict script-src policy (for example script-src 'self' without 'unsafe-inline', a nonce or a hash), the browser refuses to run this script. In my case app doesn't work at all.

## Expected
The production bootstrap is emitted either as an external script (src) or as a non-executable data block, so that script-src 'self' works without exceptions. Emitting executable inline code should not be the default.




### Provide environment information

```bash
- Next.js 16.4.3, Node 24.22.1, Pages Router
- Reproduced on a production build, not in development mode
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Output

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local)

### Additional context

Avoiding inline scripts is the safer default. A policy that bans inline script execution is a common and recommended hardening measure, and it should not be necessary to disable the policy or add `'unsafe-inline'` to run a production build.

Noncing might not be a good solution, as some CSP rules may be set by external CDNs or gateways, which the application cannot control and which cannot be relied on to pass a per-request nonce through.

title: unstable_cache: entry written after revalidateTag(tag, { expire: 0 }) is treated as fresh although its data was read before the expiry
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

No public reproduction yet; the mechanism is shown below with references to the 16.4.2 source.

### To Reproduce

1. A page reads a value through `unstable_cache(fn, keyParts, { tags: ['t'], revalidate: 60 })`; the entry is missing, so `fn` runs.
2. While that page request is in flight, a route handler changes the underlying data and calls `revalidateTag('t', { expire: 0 })`, then responds.
3. After that response, request the page again.

Locally (`next build` + `next start`, default cache handler) we fire the page load and the mutating route concurrently, then load the page once more: the old value came back in 15 of 25 attempts.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the second page load still gets the value from before the change, for up to `revalidate` seconds.

**Expected:** after `revalidateTag(tag, { expire: 0 })` has returned and its response was sent, no request is served a value whose computation started before that call.

### Analysis

- On a miss, `unstable_cache` returns the result and defers the write: `workStore.pendingRevalidates[invocationKey] = cacheNewResult(...)` (`dist/server/web/spec-extension/unstable-cache.js`), awaited only after the response.
- `FileSystemCache.set` stamps the entry with `lastModified: Date.now()` at write time (`dist/server/lib/incremental-cache/file-system-cache.js`).
- `areTagsExpired(tags, lastModified)` only treats the entry as expired if `expiredAt > lastModified`. When the deferred write lands after the `revalidateTag` call, `lastModified` is newer than the expiry and the stale value counts as fresh.

With `NEXT_PRIVATE_DEBUG_CACHE=1` the log shows `FileSystemCache: revalidateTag [ 't' ] { expire: 0 }` from the route handler followed by `FileSystemCache: set <key>` from the earlier page request.

A possible fix: stamp the entry with the time the computation started, or skip/expire the write if one of its tags was expired after the computation started.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

No minimal repro yet. It happens on one production app, only on one real device (see below). Details and a one-line workaround are below.

### Current vs. expected behavior

**Current (16.4.2, still the same code in 16.4.3 and 16.5.0-canary.27):** on an iPhone in Safari, while logged in to our app, client navigation stops working. `<Link>` taps and `router.push` show the pending state forever: the old page stays dimmed and the new route never loads. A full reload works. Logged out on the same phone, everything works.

**Expected:** navigation works, as it did on 16.2.1.

### What we found

The `?trace=1` overlay in our app records every `fetch()` the page makes, plus the segment-cache scheduler's state. During the stall:

- the prefetch scheduler sat at **4 requests in progress** (the `inProgressRequests < 4` cap) with **0 response bodies being read**;
- **no `fetch()` was ever made** for those 4 requests, so no prefetch or navigation request went out at all;
- no JS errors and no unhandled rejections.

Every router request runs through `setCacheBustingSearchParam`, which awaits `computeClientCacheBustingSearchParam` before calling `fetch`. Since the SHA-256 change, that function calls `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …)` whenever `crypto.subtle` exists:

- https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/client/components/router-reducer/set-cache-busting-search-param.ts
- https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/cache-busting-search-param.ts

On this device that promise never settled. Each of the 4 scheduler slots stayed claimed waiting for it, so the queue never moved, and navigations queued behind the prefetches.

title: experimental.inlineCss: a stylesheet sent as `<style>` in a prefetched segment and as `<link>` in the navigation crashes the navigation (React error #137)
body:
## Versions

- next 16.4.2 (production build, `next build && next start`; does not occur under `next dev`, where CSS is never inlined)
- React bundled with Next: react-dom 19.3.0-canary-278794d7-20261002
- `experimental.inlineCss: true`, `cacheComponents: true`, App Router, Turbopack build

## What happens

A client-side navigation through a `<Link>` to a dynamic route throws, and the router never commits. The address bar changes, but the previous page stays on screen. The browser reports:

```
Minified React error #137; args[]=link
  ("link is a void element tag and must neither have `children` nor use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`")
```

That error is followed by repeated `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'removeChild')`.

## Why

The destination route's segment CSS (one chunk, here `/_next/static/chunks/0fck8gdlfcliz.css`, imported by a client component in the route group's layout) reaches the client in two different forms in the same navigation.

The prefetched segment (`next-router-segment-prefetch: /view/$d$argumentId/$d$version/!KGFyZ3VtZW50KQ/__PAGE__`) carries it inlined, as a `<style>` with `precedence` and `href`:

```
["$","style","0",{"precedence":"next","href":"/_next/static/chunks/0fck8gdlfcliz.css","children":"$30"}]
30:T7b6,#mainContentDiv:has(...){...}...
```

The dynamic navigation response (`rsc: 1`, no prefetch header) carries the same file as a stylesheet link:

```
["$","link","0",{"rel":"stylesheet","href":"/_next/static/chunks/0fck8gdlfcliz.css","precedence":"next","crossOrigin":"$undefined","nonce":"..."}]
```

React's `getResource` keys both forms by the address alone. For `"style"` the key is `getStyleKey(pendingProps.href)`, and for `"link"` with `rel="stylesheet"` it is the same `getStyleKey(pendingProps.href)`, in the same `hoistableStyles` map. When the `<link>` is seen first, it registers a resource of type `"stylesheet"`. The `<style>` then finds that resource and reuses it. `acquireResource` takes its `"stylesheet"` b

title: 16.4.3: RSC flight payload serialized twice on postponed responses when partialPrefetching is enabled
body:
### Link to the original report

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/97806 — "Cache Components: the prerendered shell's RSC tree is serialized twice into the HTML" was closed by the bot for lacking a repository reproduction (and is locked, so a follow-up comment is not possible). This is a re-report with a minimal repo.

### Minimal reproduction

https://github.com/codesyslab/next-flight-payload-doubled-repro

- `next@16.4.3` + `react@19.3.1`, `next.config.mjs`: `cacheComponents: true`, `partialPrefetching: true`
- Routes: `/` (static) and `/[slug]` with `generateStaticParams` seeding the single param `seed`
- `bun install && bun run build && bun run start`, then request a NON-seeded slug: `curl -s -D - http://localhost:3200/other` → `x-nextjs-postponed: 1`

### Observed

The flight tree is serialized twice in one response — `self.__next_f` chunks `[3761, 3766]`; the second chunk starts `1c:o1,#1c:o543,2:"$Sreact.fragment"` while the first starts `1:"$Sreact.fragment"`. A prerendered request (`/seed`, `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`) emits a single chunk, and so does `/` (static).

### Control

With `partialPrefetching: false` (keeping `cacheComponents: true`) the same postponed response emits ONE chunk (`[3763]`) — the duplicated copy appears only while partial prefetching is enabled.

### Impact

Measured on a production app on the same versions (Cache Components + partial prefetching + ISR): the home document is 1 076 877 chars with a 556 921-char flight payload, of which the second copy is 257 168 chars (158 of 170 product ids occur exactly twice); `/about` is 123 741 + 123 929. Roughly a quarter of every page is the duplicated copy. Is the second serialization required by the partial-prefetching shell, and can it be deduplicated?

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

Any app on 16.4.x (reproduced on 16.4.2; the same code is on `canary` as of 16.5.0-canary.25).

### To Reproduce

1. In an app on 16.4.2, from a real terminal:
   ```sh
   __NEXT_AGENT_UPGRADE_FORCE_TERMINAL_FOR_TESTING=1 next dev
   ```
   (the testing switch only stands in for a real advisory; we first hit this with a real one on 16.4.1)
2. The upgrade menu opens (`Upgrade now` / `Skip` / `Skip until next version`).
3. Leave it alone for longer than ten seconds, and send a request to the dev server meanwhile.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected**, per `docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/agentUpgrade.mdx` (“Reminder behavior”):

> If you don't choose within ten seconds, or the buffered output grows past about 10 MiB, the reminder skips automatically.

**Current**: the menu stays open indefinitely. 75 seconds later the terminal is still on the alternate screen (`\x1b[?1049h` written, `\x1b[?1049l` never) and the request log lines are still held behind the menu. Only a key press or Ctrl+C closes it.

Reading the source, the only ten-second timeout under `lib/upgrade/` is the registry fetch (`AbortSignal.timeout(10000)` in `prepare-upgrade`). The menu in `cli/next-dev` waits on its `AbortController`, which is only aborted when the session stops.

**Why it matters more than it looks**: when `next dev` runs under a task runner that gives it a pseudo-terminal but doesn't forward keystrokes, nobody can answer the menu. Turborepo does this for any task that isn't `interactive`, and a persistent `dev` task can't be made `interactive`, because interactive tasks refuse to start outside a terminal. So `turbo run dev` stays stuck behind the menu, with its output held, for as long as the installed version has an advisory. Ctrl+C stops the whole run, and the next `turbo run dev` opens the menu again. The workaround is to run `next dev` once directly and pick “Skip until next version”. `next build` i

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue
(Minimal repro to attach: an App Router page using `next/font/google`, built twice with a persisted `.next/cache` and different `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` values.)

### To Reproduce
1. App Router project with a `next/font` font (for example `Inter` from `next/font/google`) and `deploymentId` set via `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID` (as on Vercel with Skew Protection).
2. `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID=AAA next build --webpack`
3. Keep `.next/cache`, then `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID=BBB next build --webpack`
4. Serve the second build and compare the font preload URLs (HTML `Link` header / `<link rel=preload>`) with the `@font-face` URLs inside the emitted CSS chunk.

### Current vs. Expected behavior
**Current:** the preloads use `?dpl=BBB`, but the CSS chunk produced by next-font-loader still contains `?dpl=AAA` (restored from the webpack cache). The URLs differ, so every font is downloaded twice and the preload is wasted; the font used by the page arrives late and its swap forces a full relayout.

**Expected:** the font CSS uses the current deployment id (`?dpl=BBB`).

On production (Vercel restores the build cache on every deploy) this added a full relayout of ~72k layout objects (420-1,075 ms at 4x CPU throttling) to a large page; median Total Blocking Time rose from ~1,230 ms to ~2,170 ms after the first deploy that restored a Next 16 cache.

### Cause
`packages/next/src/build/webpack-config.ts` builds the filesystem cache `version` from `__dirname`, the Next version and `configVars`, and `configVars` does not include `config.deploymentId`. next-font-loader writes `?dpl=${deploymentId}` into the CSS (`build/webpack/loaders/next-font-loader`), so its cached output is only valid for the deployment id it was built with. Present in 16.4.2 and 16.5.0-canary.23.

### Workaround
Append the deployment id to the cache version in `next.config.js`:

```js

  page.tsx              // <Link href="/photos">open</Link>
  photos/page.tsx       // full page, reads searchParams
  @modal/
    default.tsx         // return null
    (.)photos/page.tsx  // modal, reads searchParams; renders <Link href="/photos?id=1">item</Link>
```

### To Reproduce

1. `next build && next start` (self-hosted; the bug does not reproduce on Vercel).
2. Open `/`, click the link to `/photos` — the intercepted modal opens (`@modal/(.)photos`).
3. Inside the modal, click a link (or call `router.push` / `router.replace`) that changes **only the search params** of the intercepted route, e.g. `/photos?id=1`.

**Current:** nothing happens. The URL stays at `/photos`, no navigation request is sent, and the modal does not re-render. It fails deterministically (9/9 in our measurements) with `<Link>`, `router.push` and `router.replace` alike. A full document load of `/photos?id=1` works.

Interception routes are compiled into rewrites with `has: [{ type: "header", key: "next-url" }]`. In `next start`, they are applied by `dist/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.js`:

}
```

body:
Public dependency remediation request for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (CVE-2026-93687). This is an already published advisory, not a newly discovered exploit. No private repository, credentials, or customer data are needed to reproduce the installed dependency paths.

## Affected dependency path

`eslint-config-next@16.4.2 → @next/eslint-plugin-next@16.4.2 → fast-glob@3.3.1 → micromatch@4.0.8 → braces@3.0.3`

The installed plugin's `dist/utils/get-root-dirs.js` imports fast-glob and invokes `globSync(rootDir.replace(/\\/g, '/'), {onlyDirectories:true})` for string/array `settings.next.rootDir`. Without an explicit rootDir, it uses `context.cwd`; no publicly supplied request-to-glob exploit has been demonstrated. The installed dependency remains in the full audit.

## Reproduction without private code

In a disposable project with Node 24, a compatible ESLint version and `eslint-config-next@16.4.2`, run `npm ls braces --all` and `npm audit --json`. Inspect published `@next/eslint-plugin-next` package metadata and `dist/utils/get-root-dirs.js`. Test root discovery with string and array roots, `onlyDirectories`, multiple roots, backslash normalization, hidden/symlink directories, missing roots and ordering.

A small synthetic comparison of `fast-glob.globSync` and `tinyglobby.globSync` passed four `*.ts`, `*.{ts,js}`, `*`, and include/exclude cases; that does **not** establish complete root-discovery compatibility and no substitution was applied.

## Requested maintainer guidance

Is there a supported plugin release or planned change that removes this affected path while preserving flat config, core-web-vitals, React/hooks, TypeScript and existing lint rule behavior? A supported modern glob implementation or a maintained patched dependency would be preferable to downstream aliases. body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

No sandbox: the bug is in a pure sort comparator, and the Node snippet under "To Reproduce" shows it with no app at all. The app-level shape is described below it.

### To Reproduce

`FlightClientEntryPlugin.injectClientEntryAndSSRModules` sorts a page's client imports with this comparator ([source on canary](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/build/webpack/plugins/flight-client-entry-plugin.ts), around line 884):

```js
.sort((a, b) => (regexCSS.test(b) ? 1 : a.localeCompare(b)))
```

For two CSS files it returns `1` both ways (`cmp(a, b) === 1` and `cmp(b, a) === 1`), so it is not a consistent comparator. The order the CSS files come out in depends on how the sort happens to probe them, not on the import order the plugin collected.

Run with Node:

```js

const cmp = (a, b) => (regexCSS.test(b) ? 1 : a.localeCompare(b))

// A server page's client imports as the plugin collects them:
// two client components, then the page's CSS in import order.
const keys = [
  '/app/components/demo/InstantDemo.tsx',
  '/app/components/demo/DemoCall.tsx',
  '/app/components/landing/base.css',
  '/app/app/d/[slug]/page.css',
]
console.log(keys.slice().sort(cmp).filter((k) => regexCSS.test(k)))
// [ '/app/app/d/[slug]/page.css', '/app/components/landing/base.css' ]
```

The route where we hit it is a server `page.tsx` of this shape (names shortened; the comparator's result depends on the full list of the page's client imports, so a smaller app may or may not trip it):

```tsx
import InstantDemo from '@/components/demo/InstantDemo' // 'use client'
import DemoCall from '@/components/demo/DemoCall' // 'use client'
import '@/components/landing/base.css'
import './page.css'
```

After `next build` (webpack), that route's `page_client-reference-manifest.js` lists the `page.css` chunk before the `base.css` chunk in `entryCSSFiles`, and the HTML links them in that order.

body:
Could the documentation for @next/next/no-unwanted-polyfillio provide or link to a versioned, exhaustive contract of the Polyfill.io feature identifiers considered already supplied by Next.js?

The rule error page links to the supported-browsers guide, whose polyfill list is introduced as examples (including). These pages do not appear to specify exhaustive rule membership, identifier aliases, query/list normalization, or diagnostic ordering.

We are independently implementing compatible project lint policies and want to preserve complete coverage without copying or vendoring the upstream rule/helper implementation. We currently keep compatibility unqualified rather than infer a complete catalog from examples. A documented release-bound contract, or clarification of the intended public specification, would help.

This is a documentation/behavior-contract request, not a request for private artifacts or security-test execution. No customer data, credentials, repository source, or unpublished vulnerability details are included.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/lion9453/CVE-2026-96889-nextjs-rce

Control file: [`app/public/avif-control.svg`](https://github.com/lion9453/CVE-2026-96889-nextjs-rce/blob/main/app/public/avif-control.svg)

```svg
<!--ftypavif--><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1" height="1"><rect width="1" height="1"/></svg>
```

Follow-up to [GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw) / CVE-2026-96889. 15.5.28 / 16.4.1 pin `sharp ^0.35.5` but do not change sniffing. Same code is still on `canary`.

Reopened from #100298 (auto-closed: heading was `##` instead of `###`).

### To Reproduce

Default config (`dangerouslyAllowSVG: false`). Put the file at `public/avif-control.svg`, then:

```sh
curl -sD - -o /tmp/out.bin \
  'http://127.0.0.1:3000/_next/image?url=%2Favif-control.svg&w=64&q=75'
```

A file that starts with `<svg` returns 400. This one returns 200.

```js
await detectContentType(Buffer.from(
  '<!--ftypavif--><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1" height="1"/>'
))
// actual:   'image/avif'
// expected: 'image/svg+xml'
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

AVIF is matched as “bytes 4..11 == `ftypavif`, first four bytes wildcards”:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer/detect-content-type.ts

`<!--` is four bytes, so `<!--ftypavif-->` is typed `image/avif`. SVG sniffing only looks for `<?xml` or `<svg` at offset 0.

Fix: if `buffer[0] === 0x3c`, never return AVIF/HEIC; require a plausible ISO BMFF box size for `ftyp*`.

title: Turbopack: where a large app's next build spends its time, and patches that halve it
body:
Following up #98043. On a generated 2,071-route App Router app (v16.4.0), ten Turbopack patches take a cold `next build` from 63.1s to 35.8s and a warm one after one new import from 74.5s to 28.6s on 24 CPUs, with byte-identical output; on 192 CPUs a cold build goes from 121.5s to 55.5s. An eleventh patch (64), measured on top of those, takes another 3.7s (24 CPUs) and 5.3s (192 CPUs) off the Turbopack compile of a warm build after one new import.

## Results

v16.4.0 against v16.4.0 with all ten patches (15, 22, 41, 42, 52, 55, 56, 57, 59, 61), whole `next build --experimental-build-mode=compile`, median of 2, dedicated c8gd.48xlarge, page-data pool matched to the CPUs. Warm = the persistent cache restored from an earlier build of the unedited app, then N feature modules edited to add a new import each.

| Build | 24 CPUs: v16.4.0 | 24 CPUs: patched | 192 CPUs: v16.4.0 | 192 CPUs: patched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold | 63.1s | 35.8s | 121.5s | 55.5s |
| Warm, nothing changed | 48.8s | 17.0s | 55.4s | 19.1s |
| Warm, 1 new import | 74.5s | 28.6s | 94.3s | 45.0s |
| Warm, 10 new imports | 89.0s | 33.3s | 116.3s | 49.1s |
| Warm, 1,000 new imports | 115.9s | 37.9s | 156.2s | 58.0s |
| Cold, `run-turbopack` only | 44.4s | 19.1s | 91.6s | 24.8s |

The output (`.next/server` and `.next/static`, hashed) is identical in every build. On 24 CPUs, a v16.4.0 warm build is already slower than a cold one after one new import; with the patches it is faster up to 10 new imports and within a second of cold at 1,000. No minimal repository yet: the corruption is intermittent (2 corrupted startups out of 4 on the
same project). The mechanism is reproducible in isolation, see "Standalone reproduction" below.

### To Reproduce

1. Run `next dev` on an App Router project with TypeScript and a few dozen route handlers.
2. Stop it and start it again a few times. Deleting `.next/dev/types` between restarts does not prevent it.
3. After some startups, run `tsc --noEmit`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `tsc` fails only inside the generated files, for example:

```
.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts(149,34): error TS1005: ';' expected.
.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts(152,1): error TS1128: Declaration or statement expected.
.next/dev/types/validator.ts(202,1): error TS1128: Declaration or statement expected.
```

The broken `routes.d.ts` holds one complete generated document followed by the end of another one:

```ts
  interface RouteContext<AppRouteHandlerRoute extends AppRouteHandlerRoutes> {
    params: Promise<ParamMap[AppRouteHandlerRoute]>
  }
}
outeContext<AppRouteHandlerRoute extends AppRouteHandlerRoutes> {
    params: Promise<ParamMap[AppRouteHandlerRoute]>
  }
}
```

In one occurrence, the first document listed only 5 of the 68 route handlers in

The corrupted file always has exactly the byte size of the healthy one (6,393 bytes here). That fits
two `writeFile` calls running at the same time: both open the file with `O_TRUNC` before either
writes, then the shorter content lands last and the tail of the longer one stays in place.

**Expected:** the generated files are always one complete document, whatever the timing of watcher events.

`packages/next/src/server/lib/router-utils/setup-dev-bundler.ts` (checked in the published
`dist` of 16.2.4 and 16.3.5):

- `startWatcher` writes `routes.d.ts` once with an empty man

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/shward/next-repro-100149

### To Reproduce

1. `next build --turbopack && next start` (`next dev --turbopack` fails the same way).
2. Load `/`, copy the hidden `$ACTION_ID_<id>` input name from the form.
3. Post the way a browser without JS does:
   `curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/ -F '$ACTION_ID_<id>=' -F 'email=a@b.c'`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: HTTP 500.

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'bind')
    at async h (.next/server/chunks/ssr/_9e96b531._.js:1:6829)
```

Expected: 303 after the action runs. With JS on, the `Next-Action` fetch path works.

Controls: `import PgPool from "pg-pool"` or `import pg from "pg/lib/index.js"` instead of `pg`: 303.

### Provide environment information

```
Next.js 15.5.27
Bundler: Turbopack (dev and build)
Node.js 22
OS: macOS and Linux (reproduced on both)
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Turbopack, Server Actions

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local), next dev (local)

### Additional context

From the build output:
- `.next/server/server-reference-manifest.json` has `"async": true` on every action when any module in the page's action graph is async. In a bare app it is `false`.
- `pg` is a default server external. Turbopack loads it as an async ESM external, which makes the action module async.
- `decodeAction` on the no-JS path does not await the async module. The action is undefined and `.bind` throws.

In our app the root layout's logout action reaches the database module, so every no-JS form on the site returns 500. Any page is one `pg` import away from the same.

Workaround: `turbopack.resolveAlias` to a CJS shim that `require`s the package; for `sharp`, a lazy `await import("sharp")` inside the function.

title: Proxy rewrite drops an empty `_rsc` hash, so a Server Action's redirect fetch redirects to itself until "Too many redirects"
Docs (Prefetching): a dynamic route without `loading.js` is described as not prefetched, but each `<Link>` to it still sends a prefetch request
With `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`, every JS chunk a client-side navigation loads is downloaded twice (two `<script>` tags per chunk: the Turbopack loader's and React's hoistable)
body:
**Summary.** In an App Router app with `crossOrigin: "anonymous"` in `next.config`, a client-side navigation to a route that has its own client component downloads that route's JS chunk **twice** and leaves **two `<script>` tags** for it in `<head>`. The Turbopack chunk loader inserts the first tag, with `crossorigin="anonymous"` from the config and no `async` attribute. Next then renders a hoistable `<script async src>` for the same chunk as part of the segment, *without* the config's `crossOrigin`, and React only deduplicates a hoistable script against `script[async][src="…"]`, so it never recognises the loader's tag and inserts a second one. A CORS request and a no-CORS request for the same URL have different HTTP cache keys, so the second tag downloads the chunk again. In our app (300+ chunks; `crossOrigin` is set so JS Self-Profiling and LoAF attribution can read stack frames inside the chunks) a route's first visit re-downloaded its 22 chunks (about 250 KB) after the click, and the initial page load fetched 49 chunks twice (about 500 KB). The fix on the Next side is two lines, passing `renderOpts.crossOrigin` to the two hoistable `<script>` elements the way the CSS `<link>`s and the bootstrap scripts already receive it; it is on a fork branch with an e2e test (linked below).

body:
### To Reproduce

1. Use a dynamic import with a `webpackChunkName` comment, such as React Player’s YouTube import below
2. Build with `next build --webpack` and observe the named chunk
3. Build with `next build` (Turbopack) and observe that the chunk name is lost

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Switching from webpack to Turbopack in Next.js 16.4.0 loses named dynamic-import chunks because Turbopack ignores existing `webpackChunkName` comments. For example, React Player names its YouTube import:

```js
import(
  /* webpackChunkName: 'reactPlayerYouTube' */
  'youtube-video-element/react'
)
```

webpack emits `reactPlayerYouTube.<hash>.js`, while Turbopack emits a generated filename such as `1z1qq2nqxoa77.js`.

Expected: preserve existing `webpackChunkName` names when switching from webpack to Turbopack, retaining a content hash in the filename.

### Use case

Identify third-party code in browser console messages and network requests. Our Playwright tests ignore a known YouTube progress log by its chunk URL. After switching to Turbopack, the filename no longer identifies the YouTube code, requiring a broader filter.

### Additional context

An implementation was proposed in #95409, but closed without merging.

Originally posted in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/100010. Reporting here as a regression when migrating from webpack to the default Turbopack bundler.

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/ylcn91/next-turbopack-chunk-qsa-repro

A Next.js app (next 16.5.0-canary.8, Turbopack build) that renders `?n=<elements>` static elements next to 80 `next/dynamic` client widgets (one async chunk each), plus `npm run measure`, which times only the runtime's probe selector at several DOM sizes.

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repro, `npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm run build && npm start`.
2. `npm run measure` (or open `http://localhost:3123/?n=4000` in Chrome with CPU throttling 4x and record a performance profile).
3. The boot / hydration tasks show self time in `querySelectorAll` called from `doLoadChunk` → `loadChunkCached` → `loadChunkByUrlWhole`, growing with `n`.

Repro result (Chromium, CPU 4x, 82 probe calls, median of 3):

| DOM elements | Time in the probe |
|---|---|
| 761 | 30.8 ms |
| 2,261 | 76.4 ms |
| 4,261 | 115.7 ms |
| 8,261 | 229.9 ms |

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src/browser/runtime/dom/runtime-backend-dom.ts` (canary, lines ~222 and ~255) checks whether a chunk tag already exists with

```ts
document.querySelectorAll(
  `script[src="${chunkUrl}"],script[src^="${chunkUrl}?"],script[src="${decodedChunkUrl}"],script[src^="${decodedChunkUrl}?"]`
)
```

(and the `link[rel=stylesheet][href…]` equivalent for CSS). Attribute and prefix (`^=`) selectors have no fast path, so each call walks the entire document. It runs once per chunk, so the cost is O(elements × chunks) on the main thread during boot/hydration.

| Instrumented `querySelectorAll` (78 calls, real production build) | 98–116 ms |
| Same answers from a URL index, verified identical for every call | 9–19 ms |

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/chrisgeo/next-link-colon-prefetch-loop

### To Reproduce

1. App Router app, `next@16.3.8` (also tested 16.4.0 and 16.5.0-canary.7). One dynamic route `app/items/[id]/page.js` (`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`).
2. One page with 12 links: `<Link href={`/items/jira:id-${i}`}>`. The id holds `:` and is written raw in the href (not `encodeURIComponent`).
3. `next build && next start`. Open the page in Chromium, do nothing, count requests to `/items/*`.
4. Control: the same links with `encodeURIComponent(id)`, or ids with no special char: 0 requests.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: links 5 to 8 are prefetched again and again with no user action. Production build, 30 s idle, 16.3.8: 7,877 to 8,494 requests (about 2,000 per looping link, about 270 per second). Latest run on the public repro: 8,144. Links 1 to 4: 2 requests each, then stop. Same on 16.4.0 (9,138) and 16.5.0-canary.7 (9,216). It never stops while the page is open and the links are in view. All responses are HTTP 200.

Expected: one prefetch per link (a few requests), then none until the cache entry is stale (as with the encoded href and with plain ids).

In a production app (a list page, 13 rows, each row one `<Link>` to a dynamic edit route, ids like `provider:<uuid>`), one open page sent about 10,300 requests in about 2 minutes, with 4 of 13 links looping at about 100 per second each. body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/joshunger/something-here

(`next@16.5.0-canary.3`, App Router, `next build --webpack`)

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run build`
3. `npm run check`

`/` renders `EntryBox`, which imports `shared.module.css` and then `entry.module.css`.

`/other` renders `AsyncSlot`, a client component that loads `AsyncPanel` with `next/dynamic(..., { ssr: false })`. `AsyncPanel` imports `shared.module.css` and then `async-only.module.css`.

`/` does not import `AsyncPanel`. `async-only.module.css` contains the string `ASYNC_ONLY_MARKER`.

`npm run check` reads `entryCSSFiles` for the `/` entry in `.next/server/app/page_client-reference-manifest.js`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Expected: `/`'s entry CSS is `entry.module.css` plus `shared.module.css`. `async-only.module.css` is loaded with the async chunk on `/other`, not on the initial load of `/`.

Actual (default `experimental.cssChunking`, loose): `/`'s `entryCSSFiles` are

- `static/css/51855ed4fa573a0a.css` (43,205 bytes, `entry.module.css`)
- `static/css/63243da008a0aa6e.css` (51,390 bytes, contains `ASYNC_ONLY_MARKER`)

`/`'s first-load CSS is 94,595 bytes. `/other`'s own entry CSS list is empty.

`CSS_CHUNKING=strict npm run build` produces the same two files on `/`. Strict mode does not keep this stylesheet out of the entry for this graph.

Import order is part of it. In the async chunk, `shared.module.css` is immediately followed by `async-only.module.css`. If `AsyncPanel` imports `async-only.module.css` first, the marker stays out of `/`'s entry CSS. A one-line import reorder moves about 50 KiB of CSS that belongs to a dynamic import onto another route's first load.

title: Next 16.4: turbopackSharedRuntime inlines the bootstrap into the prerendered shell without a nonce, breaking hydration under a nonce CSP (cacheComponents)
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

Minimal setup, described below (I can provide a repro repository if needed).

### To Reproduce

1. Next.js 16.4.0, App Router, Turbopack production build, `cacheComponents: true`.
2. Set a per-request nonce-based CSP from middleware/proxy, following the CSP guide: `script-src 'self' 'nonce-<random>'` (no `'unsafe-inline'`).
3. Use any page whose static shell is prerendered and resumes per request (dynamic holes under Suspense).
4. Run `next build && next start` and open the page.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the page never hydrates. Two inline scripts in the prerendered shell carry no `nonce` attribute, so the browser blocks them:

- `<script id="_R_">(globalThis["TURBOPACK"] || (globalThis["TURBOPACK"] = [])).push({"otherChunks":[...],"runtimeModuleIds":[...]})</script>`, the chunk-group bootstrap emitted when `experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` is on (the 16.4 default, `getTurbopackChunkGroupBootstrap` in `app-render`)
- `<script>requestAnimationFrame(function(){$RT=performance.now()});</script>`

Every other script in the same response (the per-request part) carries the nonce correctly. Because the bootstrap is blocked, the client runtime never starts: `window.next` is undefined and nothing is interactive.

title: Turbopack: next build hangs (0% CPU, no error) when a Web Worker's module graph imports the module that spawns it
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

<PASTE the repro repository URL — contents of docs/viewer/repro/turbopack-worker-cycle>

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run build` (Turbopack, the default) → prints "Creating an optimized production build …" and never returns (0 % CPU, no error; killed after 180 s).
3. `npm run build:webpack` → finishes in ~5 s.
4. Edit `lib/work.js` so it no longer imports `lib/spawn.js` (break the cycle) → `npm run build` finishes in ~1 s.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

The app has a worker spawned with `new Worker(new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` in `lib/spawn.js`. The worker (`lib/worker.js`) imports `lib/work.js`, which imports `lib/spawn.js` — so the worker's module graph contains the module that spawns it. A client component imports `lib/work.js`.

Current: `next build` with Turbopack hangs silently.
Expected: either a build, or an error naming the cycle across the worker boundary.

Real-world instance: `@cornerstonejs/tools` 5.11.3 (`workers/computeWorker.js` → `utilities/segmentation/index.js` → `utilities/registerComputeWorker.js`, which spawns `computeWorker.js`) — any Next 16.2 app importing that package cannot be built with Turbopack without patching the package.

### Provide environment information

See `next-info.txt` in the repository (macOS 27 arm64, Node 26.5.0, Next 16.2.10).

### Which area(s) are affected?

Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected?

next build (local), Vercel (Deployments)

### Additional context

A panic log is not written; the process simply never completes. Webpack handles the same graph.

body:
## Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/mercuriumgroup/next-stale-shell-server-action-repro

## To Reproduce

1. Create a page with `cacheLife("minutes")` (a prerendered shell with revalidate = 60s) and a server action invoked from a client component.
2. Run `next build && next start`. Wait over 60 seconds so the shell is stale.
3. POST the fetch action to that page repeatedly with header `next-action: <id>`, `content-type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8`, and body `["var_id",1]`.

## Current vs. Expected behavior

With `cacheComponents` on, a server action POST to a page whose prerendered shell is stale (`isStale === true` or `-1`) reaches the background-revalidation block in `dist/build/templates/app-page-runtime.js` (also `dist/esm/build/templates/app-page-runtime.js`, which Turbopack bundles): `scheduleOnNextTick` -> `responseCache.revalidate` -> `responseGenerator({ forceStaticRender: true })`. The condition for entering that block is `supportsRDCForNavigations && (isDynamicRSCRequest || isPossibleServerAction) && !forceStaticRender`.

That re-render uses the same `req`, so `handleAction` runs a second time on an already-consumed body. Actions fail with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` (text bodies, e.g. `["var_id",1]`) or `Error: Unexpected end of form` (multipart). The log shows `MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 end listeners added to [IncomingMessage]` first. A stack trace of the second `handleAction` call goes through `ResponseCache.handleRevalidate`.

Measured result: with a stale shell, 299 of 300 sequential POSTs returned 500, and the server logged the second handler call on every request. With a fresh shell, 200 of 200 returned 200. Because the background re-render never refreshes the shell, it stays stale and the next action fails the same way. In a real app this shows up as a flaky 1-in-10 failure only because the shell is usually fresh.

Expected: a server action request never schedules a render that runs the action aga

None, this is a report against our own application. No minimal reproduction yet, see the

### What browser are you using (if relevant)?

Chromium 141 (Playwright), but the failure happens server side during compilation.

### How are you deploying your application (if relevant)?

Not deployed. `next dev` only, and that distinction turns out to matter: `next build`
compiles the exact same source without any error.

### Describe the Bug

Turbopack's dev-mode CSS pipeline emits **control characters** into the generated CSS when
compiling a Tailwind v4 arbitrary variant that contains nested attribute selectors. The
resulting stylesheet is then rejected by Turbopack's own CSS parser, so every page renders
a `Build Error` overlay instead of the application.

The class triggering it, from a shadcn/ui `field.tsx` extended locally with a `:not()`:

```
[:is(input,select,textarea,[data-slot=control],[data-slot=select-trigger]):not([aria-hidden])+&]:-mt-1.5
```

```
Parsing CSS source code failed

Unexpected token Delim('\u{7}')

title: Default experimental.cpus uses os.cpus(), which ignores container CPU limits and oversizes next build worker pools
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/server/config-shared.ts#L2396-L2400

### To Reproduce

The default for `experimental.cpus` is computed from `os.cpus()`:

```ts
cpus: Math.max(
  1,
  (Number(process.env.CIRCLE_NODE_TOTAL) ||
    (os.cpus() || { length: 1 }).length) - 1
),
```

`os.cpus()` lists the host's cores, not the ones the process may use. On Linux, run this on a 12-core host with a 2-CPU limit applied the two common ways (Node 22.23.2):

```bash
cat > probe.js <<'EOF'
const os = require('os');
console.log(`os.cpus ${os.cpus().length}, availableParallelism ${os.availableParallelism()}`);
EOF

# CPU quota, the mechanism behind `docker run --cpus=2` and Kubernetes CPU limits
systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% node probe.js
# os.cpus 12, availableParallelism 2

# CPU affinity, as with `docker run --cpuset-cpus` or taskset
taskset -c 0,1 node probe.js
# os.cpus 12, availableParallelism 2
```

So `next build` in a container limited to 2 CPUs on a 12-core host sizes its worker pools for 11 workers.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** under a CPU quota or affinity limit, the `cpus` default counts every host core. The build starts far more workers than it can schedule, and each one holds its own heap.

We measured the cost on a cold production build with browser sourcemaps (Next 12.3.4, where `cpus` also sizes the Terser minifier pool, whose threads each hold a chunk plus its sourcemap). The build ran in an 8 GB cgroup with no swap, pinned to 2 cores, with `os.cpus()` reporting 12:

| `experimental.cpus` | Peak anonymous memory | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| unset (default: 11) | 7,133 MB | 180 s |
| 2 | 5,054 MB | 151 s |

middleware-rewrites deploy test: req.url expectation differs from NextNodeServer.runApi behaviour
body:
### Summary

In `test/e2e/middleware-rewrites/test/index.test.ts`, the test "should preserve rewrite query and dynamic params in Pages API routes" expects a different `req.url` in deploy mode than in local mode:

```js
url: isNextDeploy ? '/foo/bar?key=value&added=1&extra=2' : '/foo/bar?key=value'
```

The comment says deployed proxies include the query values added by the rewrite in the URL passed to the function, while locally they are only in `req.query`.

That deploy-mode value describes the hosting proxy. It differs from what Next's own server does: #94905, which added this test, says `NextNodeServer.runApi` keeps `req.url` as the original browser-visible URL for compatibility. In our adapter, which serves the app with Next's standalone server, `req.url` has the local-mode value, so the deploy-mode assertion fails even though `req.query` is correct.

### Observed with a deployment adapter

Running the deploy tests at v16.3.5 through an adapter built on `output: 'standalone'` (webpack builds):

- `req.query` matches exactly: `{ key, added: '1', extra: '2', slug: ['bar'] }`.
- `req.url` is `/foo/bar?key=value`, so the assertion fails.

With Turbopack the file is skipped for adapter runs (#95680), so the webpack path is the only one that exercises this.

### Question

Could the deploy-mode expectation be made adapter-neutral? For example, assert only `req.query` in deploy mode, or accept either URL form when `NEXT_ENABLE_ADAPTER` is set. As written, the deploy-mode branch checks a detail of the hosting proxy rather than the behaviour described in #94905.

Happy to open a PR for whichever shape you prefer.

title: iOS back navigation skips pages due to pushState timing in App Router
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/app-router

### To Reproduce

### iOS Back navigation skips entries (App Router + pushState timing)

We’re seeing a reproducible issue on iOS 17.5+ (Safari and Chrome):

**Flow:**
Home → Catalog → Category → Product → Back → lands on Home (skips intermediate pages)

---

### Root cause (WebKit behavior)

Since iOS 17.5 / Chrome 127 on iOS, WebKit flags history entries created via `pushState` without a recent user gesture.

On back navigation it skips:
- the flagged entry
- and the previous one

(see `Document::hasRecentUserInteractionForNavigationFromJS` and `WebBackForwardList::itemStartingAtIndexSkippingItemsAddedByJSWithoutUserGesture`)

---

### Why this happens in Next.js

In the App Router, `pushState` is called in `HistoryUpdater` **after navigation commit**, not inside the user interaction handler.

Because of that, even `<Link>` navigations may be treated as non-user-initiated and get skipped in history.

---

### Workaround

We fixed it by pushing a history entry synchronously inside the user gesture using `onRouterTransitionStart` (instrumentation-client).

When Next later commits:
- it detects the same URL
- and uses `replaceState` instead of pushing again

This avoids duplicate entries and prevents WebKit from flagging the navigation.

---

### Suggested fix

Next.js could fix this by:
- calling `pushState` inside the click handler (while user gesture is active), or
- using `navigation.navigate()` where available

instead of pushing history after commit.

---

### Environment

- iOS 17.5+
- Safari / Chrome (iOS)
- Next.js 16.3.x (also reproducible in 16.4 canary)

### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Expected behavior
Back navigation should return to the previous page step-by-step:
Product → Category → Catalog → Home

### Actual behavior
Back navigation skips intermediate pages and jumps directly to Home

### Provide environment information
